item.title: Gradient-flow scale setting from octet baryon masses in N$^3$LO covariant chiral perturbation theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.33970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the gradient-flow scale $t_0$ by analyzing the lowest-lying octet-baryon masses on the Coordinated Lattice Simulations (CLS) $N_f=2+1$ ensembles in covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory up to next-to-next-to-next-to leading order (N$^3$LO). By including the finite-volume corrections self-consistently and the discretization effects from Symanzik effective field theory, we obtain a good description of the RQCD data and determine the gradient-flow scale to be $\sqrt{8t_{0,\mathrm{ph}}}=0.4120(14)_\mathrm{stat.}(16)_\mathrm{sys.}$ fm with sub-percent precision. The predicted octet baryon masses agree well with the experimental values in the isospin limit. Using the Feynman-Hellmann theorem, we also estimate the nucleon sigma terms, which are consistent with direct determinations from three-point correlation functions on the same CLS ensembles.
item.dc:creator: Xiu-Lei Ren

item.title: Parton structure of mesonic states with tensor networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.33280v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the first direct tensor network calculation of flavor-resolved parton distribution functions (PDFs) for a pion-like isospin triplet in the two-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model in (1+1) dimensions. Four-fermion interactions bind the mesons without confinement. Using staggered fermions and a charge-symmetrized Hamiltonian, we prepare the bound states and compute light-cone correlators by real-time evolution. The resulting quark and antiquark PDFs obey the expected isospin relations under $u \leftrightarrow d$ exchange between charged pions and exhibit equal u and d distributions in the neutral pion. A flavor-independent antisymmetrization of the field ordering removes the vacuum-subtracted anticommutator contribution and restores charge-conjugation relations in both the correlators and PDFs across the triplet within numerical accuracy. These results provide benchmarks for quantum simulations of the partonic structure of the meson.
item.dc:creator: Jack Y. Araz, Yamil Cahuana Medrano, Peter L. Nguyen, Zhong-Bo Kang, Jian-Wei Qiu, David Richards, Nobuo Sato, Marco Zaccheddu, Jia-Yue Zhang

item.title: Compositeness and decay properties of the flavor partner of $D^{*}_{s0}(2317)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.07171v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In view of the recent experimental finding of the heavy quark flavor partner of the $D_{s0}(2317)$ in the bottom sector, the $B_{s0}(5700)$, we perform a single and coupled-channel $B^{(*)}\bar{K}^{(*)}$ calculation in the hidden-gauge formalism within the on-shell and off-shell schemes, respectively. By fixing the $B\bar{K}$ bound state mass to the observed state with $J^P=0^+$, we also predict five new states with $J^P=\lbrace 0,1,2\rbrace^+$ in this sector, three of them with $J^P=1^+$. Additionally, in the coupled-channel calculation, two states with masses and decay widths similar to the $B_{sJ}(6114)$ and $B_{sJ}(6063)$ ones, with spins $J=0^+$ and $2^+$, respectivley, and decaying into $B\bar{K}$, are dynamically generated. Moreover, we evaluate the decay widths of the $B_{s0}$ and $B_{s1}$ states generated from $B^{(*)}\bar{K}$ through the isospin breaking decay mode $B_s^0\pi^0$ and $B_s^{*0}\pi^0$, respectively. We find that, because these states have large binding energies, the coupling to the bare component can reduce this decay width by more than half of the decay width, from $50$~keV in the purely molecular model to $10-20$~keV, when the $B_{s0}$ is coupled to the bare component. We also observe that, after considering heavy-quark-spin symmetry violating contributions, the decay width for the $B_{s1}$ becomes smaller than for the $B_{s0}$.
item.dc:creator: J. S\'anchez-Illana, R. Molina, Pan-Pan Shi

item.title: Wilsonian exact renormalization group flow in QED with the Pauli term
item.description: arXiv:2611.19778v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the renormalization group (RG) flow of quantum electrodynamics (QED) with a Pauli term, $\kappa_\tau\Bar{\psi}\sigma_{\mu\nu}F_{\mu\nu}\psi$, by using the gradient flow exact renormalization group (GFERG). In the GFERG, the gauge Ward--Takahashi (WT) identity takes the conventional form and is exactly preserved, and the gauge coupling flows only through the photon anomalous dimension~$\gamma_A$. Consequently, at any fixed point with a vanishing gauge coupling, the eigenvalue in the direction of the gauge coupling is exactly~$-\gamma_A^*$, and the gauge coupling is relevant if and only if the vacuum polarization makes~$\gamma_A^*$ negative. In the leading large-$N_f$ approximation, the vacuum polarization induced by the Pauli coupling yields such a fixed point, with~$\gamma_A^*=-1$ and three relevant directions. At finite~$N_f$, however, the $N_f$-independent one-loop effects on the fermion line eliminate it unless $N_f$ is at least several tens. For~$N_f=1$, a search over the whole plane of the Pauli coupling and the mass parameter in the subspace~$e_\tau=0$, where our flow equation is exactly of one-loop order, finds a single fixed point, at strong Pauli coupling and a finite mass parameter. Like one of the fixed points of the asymptotically safe QED proposed by Gies and Ziebell, it has a finite mass parameter and two relevant directions. At their fixed point, the gauge coupling is relevant. At ours, in contrast, $\gamma_A^*>0$, so that the gauge coupling is irrelevant, and the fixed point cannot provide a UV completion of QED with a nonzero charge. Along the full flow for~$N_f=1$ on the critical surface connected to the Gaussian fixed point, $\kappa_\tau$ is irrelevant and is attracted to an induced value proportional to~$e_\tau^3$ at weak coupling, while $e_\tau^2$ is marginally irrelevant as in QED without the Pauli term.
item.dc:creator: Sorato Nagao, Hiroshi Suzuki
